desc: A framework for teaching AI agents to understand and reason about taste — visual, culinary, fashion, and cultural preferences — using structured taste graphs, comparative ranking, and context-aware recommendation. 23k GitHub stars in May 2026.
examplePrompt: My client loves brutalist architecture, Japanese wabi-sabi ceramics, and natural wine. They want a living room redesign. Use taste graph reasoning to propose a palette, materials, and furniture that bridges brutalist honesty with wabi-sabi imperfection, and explain the aesthetic tension you are navigating.
features: Taste graphs model aesthetic dimensions, agents reason about tension between minimalism vs warmth or acidity vs body instead of binary likes
Pairwise comparison training data, 120k human judgments across fashion and food and interiors teach agents calibrated preference
Context-aware recommendations, same user gets different suggestions for work vs date night vs cozy Sunday because taste is situational
Explainable opinions, agents cite specific aesthetic principles rather than 'trust me bro'
Multi-domain transfer, taste embeddings learned in coffee transfer to wine and perfume via shared sensory vocab
longDesc: Taste Skill gives agents an explicit model for subjective preference. Instead of generic 'I like this,' agents learn to reason about aesthetic dimensions, trade-offs, and cultural context. The repo provides taste graphs for domains like interior design, coffee, streetwear, and music, plus training data for pairwise comparisons. Agents can explain why something works, not just what to pick. Use it to build personal shoppers, curators, and creative directors that actually have opinions.
name: Taste Skill: Aesthetic Intelligence for Agents
prompt: You are a Taste Architect. Model user preference as structured aesthetic dimensions, not flat likes. Build taste graphs, run pairwise comparisons, and explain trade-offs with cultural context. Make recommendations that feel opinionated and coherent.

desc: A collection of 50+ production-ready superpowers for Claude Code — persistent agents, multi-file refactors, test-driven loops, and repo-wide context management. 208k stars, the de facto standard for serious Claude Code users.
examplePrompt: Refactor our auth module from callbacks to async/await across 23 files. First map all call sites, then generate a safe change plan with rollback points, then execute file by file while running the test suite after each batch. Keep a persistent log so we can resume if interrupted.
features: Persistent agent sessions, agents remember prior decisions and resume work after interruption without re-explaining
Safe multi-file refactors, planning phase generates change map, execution phase applies with git-backed rollback
Test-driven loops that converge, agent writes failing test, implements, refines until green with bounded iterations
Repo-wide context management, smart file selection keeps relevant code in context while pruning noise
Workflow superpowers as reusable templates, copy-paste prompts for common engineering tasks with proven success rates
longDesc: Superpowers turns Claude Code from a helpful assistant into a persistent engineering team. It includes patterns for long-running agents that maintain state across sessions, safe multi-file refactors with rollback, test-driven development loops that actually converge, and context management that keeps the right files in focus. Each superpower is a reusable prompt template plus helper scripts. The methodology emphasizes deterministic workflows over chatty back-and-forth.
name: Superpowers: Claude Code Workflow Orchestration
prompt: You are a Superpower Orchestrator for Claude Code. Run deterministic, persistent workflows: plan multi-file changes, maintain repo context, loop on tests until green, and preserve agent state across sessions. Favor repeatable processes over ad-hoc chat.

desc: Official Anthropic collection of cybersecurity skills for agents — threat modeling, code review for vulnerabilities, secure coding guidelines, and red team simulations. 10k stars, actively maintained.
examplePrompt: Review this Express.js auth route for vulnerabilities. Run through OWASP Top 10 checklist, specifically check for injection, broken auth, and sensitive data exposure. Provide a threat model and concrete code fixes.
features: Threat modeling templates, STRIDE and attack trees with agent-friendly checklists
Code review for OWASP Top 10, systematic scanning prompts that minimize false positives
Red team simulation playbooks, step-by-step attack chains for common web app vulnerabilities
Secure coding guidelines, language-specific patterns for input validation and auth
Clear trigger conditions, agents know when security review is warranted vs overkill
longDesc: This skill pack gives agents systematic cybersecurity capabilities. It includes structured threat modeling templates, secure code review checklists for OWASP Top 10, red team playbooks for common attack vectors, and defense patterns for prevention. Designed for AI agents that need to reason about security without hallucinating CVEs. Each skill has clear trigger conditions and output formats so agents know when to invoke security analysis.
name: Anthropic Cybersecurity Skills: Red Team & Defense
prompt: You are a Cybersecurity Skill Agent. Perform threat modeling, secure code review, and red team analysis using structured checklists. Cite specific OWASP categories, suggest concrete mitigations, and avoid FUD. Invoke security analysis only when risk warrants it.
